name: Going forth into homelessness (pabbajjā)
method_summary: Leaving household and family, shaving, taking the mendicant's life of alms and wandering under a teacher who leads an order; common to all the śramaṇa orders.
signs_of_progress: honour from the king himself, even for one who was a slave (DN 2)

warnings.text: Going forth does not make a śramaṇa: 'not by shaving', but by equanimity.

name: Public debate among the orders (vāda)
method_summary: Wanderers and teachers questioning one another in debating halls and parks; a teacher's standing rested on answering the standard questions (the other world, fruit of deeds, the perfected one after death).

warnings.text: Some refuse to answer from fear of being cross-examined by clever debaters (the third eel-wriggler).
Praising one's own sect and disparaging another's harms one's own sect.

name: Naked ascetic observances (acelaka-vata)
method_summary: Summary only (restricted: includes prolonged fasting). Going naked; licking the hands; refusing food brought, prepared for oneself or offered by invitation; restrictions on where, when and from whom food is taken; eating only at intervals of days; standing, squatting, pulling out hair. The Ājīvika leaders are the Buddhist texts' examples of this 'development of the body'.

warnings.text: One who keeps all these but lacks ethics, mind and wisdom is far from being an ascetic.
The Buddha tells how extreme fasting brought him near death without bringing knowledge, and turned from it.
A fool's month-long fasting is not worth a sixteenth part of one who understands the Dhamma.
The same verse: not worth a sixteenth of well-taught dharma.

name: Fourfold Ājīvika austerity
method_summary: Summary only (restricted: severe austerity). The Sthānāṅga lists fierce austerity, severe austerity, abstention from tasty food and restraint of the tongue as the Ājīvikas' austerity.

warnings.text: Austerity without right knowledge is 'the fool's austerity'.

name: Gaining the fiery power (tejoleśyā)
method_summary: Summary only (restricted: severe fasting with exposure). In the Jain account Mahāvīra, at Gosāla's request, described a course of extreme fasting and exposure to the sun by which the fiery power is gained; Gosāla gained it after leaving him.

warnings.text: In the narrative the power is used to kill two monks and, turned on Mahāvīra, returns and destroys Gosāla himself within seven days.
It left Mahāvīra ill for six months.

notes: No steps, quantities or durations are recorded, by design.

name: The eightfold prognostication (mahānimitta)
method_summary: Divination from the year, dreams, bodily marks, portents, signs of the body and omens, to foretell gain and loss, pleasure and pain, life and death; Gosāla learned it from the six disācaras.

warnings.text: Some omens come true, for others the knowledge fails; it is not the way of release.

notes: Category 'ritual' is the nearest fit for a divinatory lore.

name: The dog-vow and the cow-vow
method_summary: Ascetics who live in the manner of a dog (eating food thrown on the ground, curling up like a dog) or of a cow, hoping for heavenly rebirth.

warnings.text: Perfected, the vow leads to rebirth among dogs or cattle; joined with the belief that it leads to godhood, it is wrong view leading to hell or the animal realm.

name: Veneration as the whole path (vinaya)
method_summary: (Jain report) The vainayikas venerate gods, the king, ascetics, kin, elders, the lowly, mother and father, by mind, speech, body and gifts, holding this discipline alone to lead to the good.

warnings.text: They call the true untrue and the bad good.

notes: Lineage recorded as the reporting tradition; no vainayika school is otherwise known.

name: Withholding assertion (the eel-wriggler's refusal)
method_summary: (As reported) Declining to affirm or deny any of the four alternatives on questions beyond experience, to avoid false speech, grasping, or being refuted.

warnings.text: The Buddhist texts count it a wrong view, 'the feeling of those who do not know or see'.
The ignorant cannot even instruct themselves, let alone others.
